title: `AppTest.switch_page()` cannot navigate to an `st.navigation` page that sets a custom `url_path`
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`AppTest.switch_page(page_path)` computes the target page hash from the page's **file
name**. But `st.navigation` identifies each `st.Page` by its **`url_path`**. When a page
sets a custom `url_path` that differs from its file name, the two hashes disagree:
`switch_page` sets a `_page_hash` that matches no registered page, and the script runner
**silently falls back to the default page** instead of navigating to the requested one (and
without raising).

This makes it impossible to test navigation to any page declared like
`st.Page("other.py", url_path="custom")`.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
See below.
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Files (all in one directory):

`home.py`
```python
import streamlit as st

st.write("HOME PAGE")
```

`other.py`
```python
import streamlit as st

st.write("OTHER PAGE")
```

`app.py`
```python
import streamlit as st

home = st.Page("home.py", default=True)
other = st.Page("other.py", url_path="custom")  # url_path != file name ("other")

st.navigation([home, other]).run()
```

`test_switch_page.py`
```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest


def test_switch_to_page_with_custom_url_path():
    at = AppTest.from_file("app.py").run()
    assert at.markdown[0].value == "HOME PAGE"

    at.switch_page("other.py").run()

    assert at.markdown[0].value == "OTHER PAGE"  # FAILS: is "HOME PAGE"
```

Run pytest:
```
$ pytest test_switch_page.py
E       AssertionError: assert 'HOME PAGE' == 'OTHER PAGE'
```

### Expected Behavior

`at.switch_page("other.py").run()` renders the `other` page (or, if the path can't be resolved to a registered page, raises a clear error).

### Current Behavior

The default page is rendered, silently.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: 3.13.15
- Operating System: Linux (WSL2) — also expected on macOS/Windows; not platform-specific


### Additional Information

#### Root cause

`AppTest.switch_page` derives the hash from the file name
(`streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py`):

```python
page_path_str = str(full_page_path.resolve())
_, page_name = page_icon_and_name(Path(page_path_str))
self._page_hash = calc_hash(page_name)          # hash of the FILE NAME
```

but `st.navigation` registers each page under a hash derived from its `url_path`
(`streamlit/navigation/page.py`):

```python
[USER]
def _script_hash(self) -> str:
    return calc_hash(self._url_path)             # hash of the URL PATH
```

`self._url_path` defaults to the file-name-derived slug, so the two hashes coincide **only
when `url_path` is not overridden**. With a custom `url_path`, `calc_hash(page_name)`
matches no registered page, so the runner uses the default page instead.

#### Suggested fix

Resolve the requested page against the app's registered navigation pages (via the
`PagesManager` / `st.navigation` result), matching by resolved script path, and use that
page's actual `_script_hash` (which respects `url_path`) for `_page_hash`. Because the
navigation config is only known once the app runs, this can be done by deferring resolution
to the next `run()` (store the requested path in `switch_page`, resolve it against the
freshly built pages when running).

At minimum — even without full resolution — `switch_page`/`run` should **raise a clear
error when the computed hash matches no registered page**, rather than silently rendering
the default page, so the failure is not hidden from test authors.

#### Workaround

Set `_page_hash` to the `url_path`-based hash directly for the affected pages:

```python
from streamlit.util import calc_hash

at._page_hash = calc_hash("custom")  # the page's url_path
at.run()
```

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16611)

`AppTest.switch_page()` hashes the **file-name slug** (`calc_hash(page_name)` from `page_icon_and_name`), while `st.Page._script_hash` hashes the page’s **`url_path`**. Those hashes match only when `url_path` is left as the inferred filename; a custom `url_path` produces a hash that matches no registered page. `PagesManager._resolve_page_script` then silently falls back to the default page (`send_page_not_found` only enqueues a proto; AppTest does not raise). This is a real testing-framework bug, not a product-API issue. A robust fix is to resolve the requested script path against pages registered by `st.navigation` and use that page’s `_script_hash`, and/or raise when the computed hash is unknown.

### Related Issues

- [#9446](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9446) — AppTest originally failed to render `st.navigation` pages at all (now closed; callable-page coverage landed). This issue is a remaining gap: file pages with a custom `url_path` still cannot be reached via `AppTest.switch_page()`.
- [#10572](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10572) — `st.switch_page` / `st.page_link` identify pages by `url_path` and can silently land on the wrong page instead of erroring. Same identity/fallback pattern as this AppTest hash mismatch.
- [#8154](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8154) — AppTest page-path resolution (relative `st.page_link` paths). Related AppTest multipage-path handling, not a duplicate.
